exposure: Type of Cesarean scar pregnancy (Type I, II, III)
High-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) combined with ultrasound-guided suction curettage
outcome: Time for serum b-HCG to return to normal levels
Rate of using Foley catheter balloon
cohort: The study included 153 patients diagnosed with type I, II, or III Cesarean scar pregnancy (CSP).
finding: HIFU combined with ultrasound-guided suction curettage is a safe and effective treatment for patients with type I/II/III CSP who desire fertility, with Type III CSP requiring more intensive management and greater dependence on Foley catheter balloon compression therapy.
mod_finding: Type III Cesarean scar pregnancies, which are a sequela of prior Cesarean birth, were associated with higher total energy used for ablation, longer treatment and sonication times, and a greater need for Foley catheter balloon compression for hemostasis compared to Type I and II CSPs.
